title: Why do summer flights get delayed more? The operational reasons
summary: One late aircraft can delay flights all day. Learn why summer delays cascade — and if yours could be worth up to €600.
body_markdown:
If you flew this summer and your flight ran late, there's a good chance it wasn't random — and there's a real chance you're owed up to €600 for it. A lot of summer delays trace back to one specific thing: a single late aircraft earlier in the day, quietly pushing every later flight behind it. Here's how that works, and how to tell if yours qualifies.


## What's actually causing the delays?


Summer delays usually come from the same three pressures compounding at once: more frequent thunderstorms, airports and airspace running close to full capacity, and knock-on scheduling effects. The first two get most of the attention. The third is the one passengers almost never hear explained — and it's often the actual reason behind a "vague" delay at the gate.


## Why does one delay turn into a whole day of delays?


Take Elena, flying Palma to Amsterdam on a Friday evening in July. Her 6:40pm departure was delayed to 9:15pm. The gate agent blamed "operational reasons" — no storm, no strike, nothing on the news. What actually happened: the same aircraft had flown Amsterdam–Palma–Amsterdam–Palma earlier that day, and its very first rotation left Amsterdam 40 minutes late because of a knock-on delay from the day before. Every leg after that ran the same 40 minutes behind, then slipped further as the airport got busier through the afternoon. By the time it reached Elena's flight, a single morning delay had grown into a two-and-a-half-hour one.


Crews have legal duty-time limits too, so a long-enough delay can mean a crew "timing out" and needing a replacement, adding yet another delay on top. That's the mechanism behind most "vague" delay reasons at the gate.


## What does this mean for you as a passenger?


If your delay caused you to miss a connecting flight booked on the same ticket, you're covered by the same rules as any other delay — our guide on[missed connections and your rights](https://www.airhelp.com/en-int/blog/i-ve-missed-my-flight-what-are-my-rights-as-a-passenger/) walks through what happens next. If you booked your connection as a separate ticket, the airline isn't obligated to rebook you; our guide to[self-connecting flight rights](https://www.airhelp.com/en-int/blog/what-are-your-rights-for-self-connecting-flights/) explains where you stand.


## Which of these delays can you actually claim for?


Not all of them. Weather and air traffic control restrictions are usually treated as extraordinary circumstances, so no compensation is owed. But delays caused by a late-arriving aircraft or a crew scheduling issue — like Elena's — sit within the airline's control. Landing 3 hours or more late on a cause like that means you could be entitled to up to €600 under EC261.


For the fuller picture across every kind of summer disruption — including strikes, with two real examples and verdicts — see our guide to[peak-summer delays](https://www.airhelp.com/en-int/blog/peak-summer-delays-why-july-and-august-are-the-worst-and-what-you-can-claim/) . To check your specific flight, use our[flight delay compensation guide](https://www.airhelp.com/en-int/flight-delay-compensation/) .


## FAQ


#### Why are there more flight delays in summer?


Because weather, capacity, and knock-on scheduling effects all peak in the same months — not because of one single cause.


#### What's a "knock-on" flight delay?


It's when a delay on one flight carries over to the next flight that same aircraft or crew is scheduled for, and the next one after that — so a single early delay can still be affecting flights hours, or even a full day, later.


#### Can a delay from earlier in the day still affect my flight?


Yes. If your aircraft flew earlier routes that day, a delay on any of those can still be rippling through the schedule by the time it reaches your flight — even once the original cause has cleared.


#### What should I do if my flight is delayed in summer?


Check the AirHelp app for your rights in real time, ask the airline for meals or accommodation if you're entitled to them, and keep your boarding pass and any delay notices as proof.
